alt: Poster: Jio Platforms lists on NSE and BSE - issue price Rs 1,119, listing price Rs 1,358, listing premium 21.36%, 28 Oct 2026
text:
Jio Platforms made its market debut on 28 October, listing at a premium to its IPO price on both NSE and BSE.

• The shares listed at Rs 1,358 on NSE and BSE against an issue price of Rs 1,119, a premium of about 21.36%, per HDFC Sky and Analytics Insight reports of exchange data.
• The issue price was the top of the Rs 1,065-1,119 price band, and the IPO was a fresh issue with no offer-for-sale component, per HDFC Sky.
• Benchmarks ended slightly lower, with the Nifty near 22,700, as IT and energy shares declined, per Business Standard and Kotak Neo.
• Nifty Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 ended higher, up about 0.4% and 0.9%, per Kotak Neo.

Our view: a listing-day premium reflects demand at one point in time and says little about what the shares may do later. Participants usually look at valuation, business mix and subsequent liquidity rather than the debut move alone, and a single session is a thin basis for conclusions. This is an interpretation of the data, not a prediction or advice, and we do not comment on whether to buy or sell any security.

For practitioners: when a very large IPO lists at a sizeable premium, which post-listing data points (delivery volumes, index inclusion timelines, lock-in expiries) do you find most informative?
